0.long_answer: The specialized procedure is known as the EXIT (ex utero intrapartum treatment) procedure. This technique is specifically used to manage cases where a fetus has airway compression due to large congenital lesions such as CPAM. During an EXIT procedure, the baby is partially delivered via cesarean section while still attached to the umbilical cord, allowing the placental circulation to continue. This provides the surgical team with a critical window of time to secure the baby’s airway before complete delivery, reducing the risk of hypoxia and ensuring a smoother transition to independent life. It is a highly complex and carefully orchestrated procedure performed by a skilled fetal surgery team.
